summary: Added #[Group('live-http')] PHP attribute (PHPUnit 13 style) to AjaxRequestTest class and to RequestTest::test_adapterSockets and test_adapterCURL. Added <groups><exclude><group>live-http</group> block to phpunit.xml so the default suite skips them automatically. Documented the live-http group in testing.md including the composer test-group command to run them explicitly. Updated both test files to import PHPUnit\\Framework\\Attributes\\Group.

comments.note: PHPUnit 13 dropped @group docblock annotation support in favour of PHP 8 attributes (#[Group(...)]). Using the legacy @group annotation would silently have no effect in PHPUnit 13, causing the tests to remain in the default group. The fix uses #[Group('live-http')] with the PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\Group import. Any other test classes in the project that use @group annotations for filtering should be migrated to attributes.
AjaxRequestTest had no class-level docblock before this change. A minimal docblock explaining that this class makes live HTTP requests was added alongside the #[Group] attribute.

summary: Live-HTTP group isolation verified. AjaxRequestTest has class-level #[Group('live-http')] PHP attribute (PHPUnit 13 style) with correct Group import. Full suite (996 tests) exits 0 confirming AjaxRequestTest and live-http RequestTest methods are excluded by default. summary: WP-003: The PHPUnit group isolation implementation is correct and follows PHPUnit 13 conventions precisely. Using #[Group('live-http')] PHP 8 attributes with the PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\Group import is the right approach — the legacy @group docblock annotation is silently dropped by PHPUnit 13. Class-level attribute on AjaxRequestTest correctly marks all methods in the class. Method-level attributes on test_adapterSockets and test_adapterCURL in RequestTest correctly leave the other non-live methods in that class in the default group. phpunit.xml exclusion is the right mechanism to prevent CI failures. The testing.md documentation is comprehensive and actionable. Minor: the testing.md prose uses '@group live-http' (annotation style) in the description text at line 283-284 while the actual code uses the attribute style — a cosmetic inconsistency but not a functional problem.

comments.note: testing.md lines 283-284 and 286 use '@group live-http' in descriptive prose while the actual implementation uses #[Group('live-http')] attributes. The table and command example are correct.
